caption:
Mississauga condo? Surprise bill coming?

Buying a resale condo in Mississauga? 1) Ask the condo corporation for the status certificate; anyone can request it. 2) The corporation can charge up to $100 including tax and must provide it within 10 days. 3) Read the budget, the statement on the reserve fund and any special assessments charged to the unit. 4) Look for unpaid fees on the unit and any outstanding judgments or ongoing lawsuits against the corporation. 5) Have your lawyer review it before your condition date.

Source: Condo Authority of Ontario, status certificates page (read Nov 4, 2026).

Brampton new build? Is your deposit safe?

Deposit protection on new Ontario homes has limits. 1) Freehold, price $600,000 or less: Tarion deposit coverage is up to $60,000. 2) Over $600,000: 10% of the price, up to a maximum of $100,000. 3) Register your purchase agreement with Tarion; Tarion says purchasers who register within 45 days qualify for the maximum coverage. 4) Reservation or hold payments made before signing are not covered. 5) Condo deposits must be held in trust; if they were not, Tarion covers up to $20,000.

Source: Tarion, deposit protection pages (read Nov 4, 2026).

Buying a new build in Brampton? Want the full step-by-step list? Comment CHECKLIST for my free buyer checklist, or call 905-452-4298.

General information only, not legal, tax or mortgage advice. Tarion has announced changes to freehold deposit coverage, deferred to January 1, 2027; confirm current rules with Tarion and your lawyer.

Kitchener inspection passed? Not everything's checked.

Before your inspection condition ends: 1) Read the limitations section; most reports list what couldn't be inspected. 2) Ask which areas were locked or blocked, like attics or crawl spaces. 3) For an older home, ask whether a qualified tradesperson should check the wiring, plumbing or sewer line. 4) Your insurer may ask about the age of the wiring, plumbing and heating. 5) Get your answers before the condition date, not after.

Milton showing: what can you miss?

Picture this: you have 10 minutes inside a Milton home. 1) Look up: check ceilings for stains, peeling paint and cracks near corners. 2) Open and close every door and window; sticking ones may point to moisture or movement. 3) Run the taps, flush the toilets and sniff for musty odours. 4) Take photos, then ask your Realtor to follow up on anything odd.
